_meta.voice: Voice v2 — second person, present tense, short lines, dry needle. The chair needles the choice, never the kid.
_meta.chair: The suited shark mascot. Chairs the panel, narrates the run, owns the Shark Respect meter.
_meta.placeholders: {rev} {burn} {runway} {cash} {valuation} {year} {company} {n}. Shark reaction lines are deliberately placeholder-free — they are spoken in-scene.
_meta.rule: score_low and react_low roast the pitch's logic and decisions only — never voice, accent, energy, or the founder.

welcome: Five sharks. One camera. Sixty seconds of you. Start when the light turns.
The panel already read your brief. They already decided what to doubt. Change their minds.
This is where a company stops being a company and becomes an argument. Make yours.
{company} walks in worth {valuation}. What it walks out with is the next four minutes' problem.
listening: The room is quiet. That isn't agreement. That's note-taking.
Marcus is running your arithmetic while you talk. He is faster than you.
Keep going. Every sentence without a number costs you something.
deliberating: They're talking about you in the third person now. That's the job.
Offers get built in silence. Yours is being priced right now.
Nobody has said no. Nobody has said yes. Hold still.
score_high: You answered the question they actually asked. You would be surprised how rare that is.
Structure, numbers, a clear ask. The panel wants in, and the panel hates wanting things.
That pitch had a spine. Respect moves up, and Respect does not move often.
You made {valuation} sound like a discount. That is the entire trick.
score_mid: A real business, argued halfway. You left money on the table and they picked it up.
Half your numbers landed. The other half you rounded and hoped nobody checked.
You got an offer. You also got the terms people get when they hesitate.
Fundable, and priced for the doubt. Both of those happened in the same four minutes.
score_low: No market size, no unit economics, no ask. Three holes, and you walked through all of them.
Your growth plan was more customers. That is a wish with a budget attached.
You priced the company on hope. They price on cash flow. Nobody met in the middle.
You asked for money and never said what it buys. That is why every one of them passed.
year_survived: Year {year} closes and you're still solvent. The bar is on the floor. You cleared it.
Another year on the books. Runway: {runway}. The calendar resets. The math doesn't.
You end at {valuation}. The panel will want to know exactly what changed and why.
Year {year}, survived. Most companies that started when you did are already footnotes.
respect_up: Respect: up {n}. The shark does not hand those out for showing up.
{n} points of Respect. It carries between runs, and so does the record of how you earned it.
The meter moves {n}. You argued a number and won it. Do that again.

react_high: You answered a numeric question with a number. Inside two seconds. That buys you my attention.
Your payback period ties out against the brief. I checked it twice while you were still talking.
Revenue is vanity, margin is sanity, cash is reality. You led with the third one. Good.
react_mid: Top line's fine. The unit economics are a rumor. Fix one of those before the next quarter.
You know your revenue cold and your CAC not at all. That's half a founder.
Numbers don't have moods. Yours went vague at exactly the place where the cash leaks.
react_low: You're buying revenue for more than it returns. That isn't growth. That's a subsidy with a logo.
Four minutes. No gross margin, no churn, no payback period. I priced what you didn't say.
Your ask rests on a multiple you heard somewhere. That isn't a valuation. That's a guess wearing a dollar sign.

react_high: You didn't hand me a product, you handed me a wedge. I can see the second market from here.
That's a trajectory, not a company. I'm already doing the ten-year math and I like the shape of it.
I asked what this looks like at a hundred times, and you gave me a mechanism instead of a hope. Keep going.
react_mid: The story is real. The ceiling is low. Show me the room above this one.
You defended the market with the market's own numbers and then stopped. Stopping is the whole problem.
I believe the curve. I don't yet believe the size of the field you drew it on.
react_low: Your entire plan is a slightly bigger slice of a shrinking pie. Small market, small dreams. I'm out either way.
You just pitched me a beautiful version of the last five years. I only buy the next five.
Every growth number in there was bought with a discount. Kill the coupon and the curve dies with it.

react_high: You walked me through the whole line without notes. That tells me you've actually stood on it.
You named the bottleneck before I asked, and then you named the fix. That's rare and I'm saying so.
Show me the machine, not the dream. You opened with the machine. That's the right order.
react_mid: The product ships. The process behind it is one person, and that person is you.
Good hands, no bench. Your number two hire happens before any other hire happens.
You've built something real and tied it to yourself with a knot. At triple the volume, you're the bottleneck.
react_low: You outsourced the one part of this you should own. Ideas are free. Execution costs everything, and you rented yours.
I asked what snaps first at ten times the volume and you told me it scales smoothly. Nothing scales smoothly.
You can't tell me how the thing gets made or who touches it on the way out. If you can't walk the floor, I can't fund the factory.

react_high: You told me why they leave, in their words, not yours. That's the answer I almost never get.
A named customer, a real moment, and a cohort number underneath it. Now I'm listening properly.
Growth is rented. Love is owned. You've quietly been buying the second one for two years.
react_mid: You have a story and no cohort. Bring me January's buyers and tell me who's still paying in June.
Lovely brand, leaky bucket. Fix the drain before you turn the tap up any further.
Four minutes on features, one on customers. Flip that ratio and the pitch changes completely.
react_low: Everything you called growth was new customers replacing the ones you lost. That's a treadmill with a marketing budget.
You don't know your repeat rate. That's the one number I never forgive, and it isn't a small thing to be missing.
Take the coupon away and there's nothing underneath. You've built a discount with a logo on it.

react_high: You led with your worst number and its cause. You just saved us both twenty minutes.
I attacked it three ways and it held. I withdraw the objection, and I don't withdraw things.
You corrected my arithmetic with evidence. Noted, out loud, on the record.
react_mid: One figure in that pitch disagrees with your own brief. I'll let it sit and see whether a second one arrives.
Your largest customer is a fifth of revenue on a month-to-month contract. Help me with the math on the day they leave.
You answered the question next to the one I asked. Precision costs nothing. Try some.
react_low: Two of your claims contradict your own brief. I can read the ledger out loud, or you can.
You called the regulatory risk manageable and then managed to say nothing about it. I believe you believe that.
The moat you described is a head start. Head starts expire, and yours already has a date on it.
